title: Freeze CCP2 synchronization and freshness traces
description:
Scope: CCP2 synchronization/adoption fixtures in /home/mark/Developer/lichen-workspace/project-LICHEN/test/vectors/, with signed-object references from the independently frozen wire family. Specify ordinary-data-not-beacon, invalid signature, malformed beacon, retired signer, stale generation, wrong time provenance, below-floor time, exact missed/recovery counts, interrupted recovery, root/generation transitions and SFN wrap. Use the adopted time-quality ordering from /home/mark/Developer/lichen-workspace/project-LICHEN/spec/09-packets-timing.md. Do not infer validity from a generic authenticated frame or implement the production FSM.

HPC8 execution policy: Code, test, or schema changes require three independent correctness, security, and robustness reviews; file and fix all findings and re-review. Use independent oracles, never weakened legacy tests or self-generated expected results. Preserve upstream Yggdrasil addressing, radio-owned identity, best-effort custody, baseline SCHC, and the human-only OSCORE/EDHOC security edit bar. External actions, hardware/RF operations, and port access require scoped explicit permission and applicable bench safety checks. Research may conclude no-go; an authorization gate requires affirmative, recorded approval for its actual scope. Dependency closure and decomposition are not permission. No speculative activation, including deferred portability or experimental modes.
design: Keep link replay, schedule generation, SFN projection and time authority distinct. Reuse unchanged primitive traces only after checking their policy revision; no legacy closure note substitutes for CCP2 transitions.
acceptance_criteria: Independent state tables pin loss of synchronization at exactly three missed valid beacon opportunities and recovery only after three consecutive qualified beacons. Invalid or ordinary-data events cannot reset freshness or recovery counters. Generation/root changes and interrupted recovery have explicit expected outcomes, and invalid objects do not mutate adopted clock/schedule state. Every trace validates against the strict schema and cites the relevant signed fixture or independently declared timing input.
